counterfactual_missing_items: Normal haptoglobin, fibrinogen, vitamin B12, folate, and copper levels
decisive_items: sustained a dog bite on her right thumb approximately one week before admission
Gram stain showed thin, fusiform gram-negative rods in two of four bottles
Nonblanchable, petechial rash over bilateral lower extremities to the level of the knees
response.rationale: C1 and R3 both capture the essential Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis diagnosis, but C1 is more complete by explicitly including the dog bite as the source. The gram-negative rods on blood culture and the dog bite history are pathognomonic. Other candidates are contradicted by the absence of schistocytes (TTP/DIC) and normal fibrinogen (DIC).

rejected.why: TTP is contradicted by the absence of schistocytes on peripheral smear and the presence of an infectious source.
DIC is unlikely given normal fibrinogen and haptoglobin, and absence of schistocytes.
GI bleeding does not explain the fever, rash, or gram-negative bacteremia; macrocytosis and low iron are likely due to alcohol use and chronic disease.
